A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VDW-GNN research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including alignment of v2 Appendices E–G with v3 Appendices F–H.

before.justification: V2 reports original ellipsoid prediction, wind reconstruction, and neural representation-learning experiments in Section 4, with results in Tables 1–6 and Figure 5.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes, including the experimental appendices.

M1.justification: The local PCA construction, vector diffusion operator, wavelet filters, architectures, and losses are retained. The corrected wind-model description matches v2 Appendix F. New Appendix E discusses possible alternatives without establishing changes to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ellipsoid diameter and node-vector tasks, masked and rotated wind reconstruction, and inductive neural representation learning. No additional dataset, population, or evaluated scenario appears.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–4, including the ellipsoid non-equivariant ablation, DD-TNN for wind reconstruction, and MARBLE, CEBRA, and LFADS for neural recordings. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The experimental appendices retain the same splits, preprocessing, model configurations, training settings, and evaluation procedures. The 2000-point wind sample with k=3, rotation tests, and inductive trial-wise neural evaluation are unchanged.

E4.justification: The non-equivariant ablation, rotation tests, and equivariance illustrations are retained. The new local PCA discussion proposes mitigation strategies but supplies no additional robustness experiment, sensitivity analysis, or ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-fold cross-validation for ellipsoids, five wind repetitions with distinct sampling and rotation seeds, and neural results across 44 days. Standard-deviation reporting and Figure 5's paired Wilcoxon tests are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–6 and the plotted results are unchanged. New Appendix E adds a brief qualitative tuning observation that wind information was highly local and best captured with k=3; it supplies no additional scores or performance improvement.

T1.justification: New Appendix E states conditional convergence in probability for a heat-semigroup wavelet alternative with fixed learnable parameters, invoking Battiloro et al. (2024). It leaves convergence of the implemented Q-power construction open. The existing theorems and proof arguments are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing vector diffusion wavelets, establishing frame and equivariance properties, and demonstrating effective geometric learning on synthetic and real data.

C2.justification: New Section 5 and Appendix E substantially expand applicability boundaries: sparse-neighborhood PCA reliability, coupled graph/wavelet tuning, manifold-assumption violations, and unresolved convergence of the implementation. Section 4.1 also adds a multiscale explanation for the stronger graph-level diameter results.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the concatenated wind-model inputs from neighbors' 3D coordinates to wind vectors and edge weights, resolving an inconsistency with the existing appendix description. Hardware, hyperparameters, software, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 substantially broadens research positioning through residual and jumping-knowledge alternatives, classical Euclidean scattering, generalized graph wavelets, robust tangent-space estimation, and continuum-convergence literature. These additions extend several substantive background discussions beyond the bibliographic updates to retained works.

P1.justification: V3 makes sentence-level corrections and localized paragraph rewrites throughout the main text. It adds Limitations and Impact Statement sections and inserts Appendix E, updating subsequent headings and cross-references. The existing explanatory sequence and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The same five figures and six tables are retained without substantive redesign. Figures and tables shift relative to surrounding text, runtime Tables 5–6 occupy separate pages, captions receive small edits, and the first page adds proceedings information.

improvement.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E make applicability limits and the unresolved convergence question clearer, while broader context and the corrected wind-model description improve explanatory precision. These are useful gains, but the experimental evidence and existing proofs remain materially unchanged.
